title: No way to open a project read-only: Save can write over a reference copy

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happened**

CamCraft cannot open a project read-only. Every open project saves over its own file:

- In the window, Save writes to the file that was opened (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3436-3440` on `main` 60b19abe8).
- The MCP tool `save_project` without a path, and the script call `cam.save()`, write to the file that was opened (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41-52`).
- `camcraft-ui` has no read-only option. `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` stops with `unknown option '--read-only'` (`crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs:192`).
- The MCP tool `open_project` takes only `path`. `open_project {"path": "job.camproj", "read_only": true}` is refused with `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:115-123`).

These users need a project that opens without a risk to its file:

- a user who opens a shipped example or a tester kit to look at it;
- a person who reviews a released job;
- a team that keeps reference copies on a shared folder.

CamCraft already has this behaviour for shipped machines. The machine editor refuses Save for a shipped machine, and Save As writes a copy (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:35-36`, `:229-242`, `:259`).

**Expected**

- `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only.
- A save over the opened file is refused on every save route: the window, MCP `save_project` and script `cam.save`. The file stays byte for byte.
- Save As to another file works, and the project is then no longer read-only.
- The title bar says that the project is read-only.
- An agent can open a project read-only with `open_project {"path": ..., "read_only": true}`.

An open SolidCraft pull request adds the same option, `solidcraft --read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830). The same name and behaviour in both apps help users who use the two.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Copy a project file, for example a shipped example, to a folder.
2. Run `camcraft-ui --read-only <copy>.camproj`. The start stops with `unknown option '--read-only'`.
3. Run `camcraft-ui <copy>.camproj`. Change a parameter and push Save. CamCraft writes over the copy.
4. In `camcraft-cli mcp`, call `open_project {"path": "<copy>.camproj", "read_only": true}`. The call is refused: `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"`.

I found this by code inspection.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at 60b19abe8 (2026-11-22). Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- A new start option `--read-only` in the option table (`cli_options.rs`). It applies to the one project file on the command line. A model file is imported as usual, because an import makes a new project with no file. A headless start ignores it.
- One rule in `crates/app/src/project/`, `project::refuse_read_only_save`, next to `project::save` and its other refusals. It refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The window's `save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it. `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP seam of a window.
- The rule compares files, not spellings (canonical paths), because the Save As dialog gives an absolute path.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as the shipped-machine editor does. A save to the opened file from the dialog is refused on the status line.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- MCP `open_project` gets an optional `read_only` boolean. Scripts get it through `cam.call("open_project", ...)`. The live seam still refuses `open_project`, but the window's read-only state reaches a live `save_project`.
- The title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.
- No file-format change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.

**Done means:** `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only and the title says so. Tests show that a save over the opened file is refused, and that the file stays byte for byte, through the window, MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live seam. Tests show that a save to another file works and ends read-only. A test shows that the option parses and keeps the file argument. The help text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`, the site guide and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` describe it.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.
